title: Isaiah Chapter 60 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 60 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 60 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 60.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:1 instruct the people to do?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:1 begins with the command to 'Arise, shine; for thy light is come'.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:2, what shall cover the earth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:2 states that 'the darkness shall cover the earth'.

questions.question: Who will come to the light according to Isaiah 60:3?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:3 says, 'And the Gentiles shall come to thy light'.

questions.question: What will the abundance of the sea be converted into according to Isaiah 60:5?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:5 mentions that 'the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee'.

questions.question: What type of animals will cover the people in Isaiah 60:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:6 states, 'The multitude of camels shall cover thee'.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 60:4 mentions that sons and daughters will gather together.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:4 states that 'thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side'.

questions.question: What will happen to the nation that does not serve the people according to Isaiah 60:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:12 declares, 'For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish'.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:14, who will come bending to the people?
options: The sons of them that afflicted thee
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of them that afflicted thee
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:14 mentions that 'the sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee'.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will be an everlasting light according to Isaiah 60:19.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:19 states, 'but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light'.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:11 say about the gates?
options: They will be closed at night
They shall be built of gold
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:11 declares, 'Therefore thy gates shall be open continually'.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 60:20 says that the sun will go down.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:20 states, 'Thy sun shall no more go down', indicating the sun will not go down.

questions.question: In Isaiah 60, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:1 gives the first instruction: 'Arise, shine; for thy light is come'.

questions.question: What will the LORD bring instead of brass according to Isaiah 60:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:17 states, 'For brass I will bring gold'.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 60:15 describes a place that has been forsaken and hated.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:15 mentions, 'Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated'.

questions.question: What will happen to the days of mourning according to Isaiah 60:20?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:20 says, 'the days of thy mourning shall be ended'.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 60 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 60 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the nations and kingdoms that do not serve thee according to Isaiah 60?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:12 states that 'For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.' This indicates the consequences of not serving the people of God.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:10, what will the sons of strangers do?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:10 mentions, 'And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls...' indicating their supportive role in the restoration and building of the community.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:16 indicate about the relationship between the LORD and His people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:16 states, 'and thou shalt know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer,' emphasizing God's role as a protector and redeemer for His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 60:14 describe the response of those who previously afflicted God’s people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:14 tells us, 'The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee...' indicating a reversal of their previous attitudes towards God's people.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:9 promise about the isles and ships of Tarshish?
options: They will bring your sons from far
questions.correctAnswer: They will bring your sons from far
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:9 states, 'Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far...' signifying a return and restoration for the people.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:5, what will happen to the people's hearts when they see the abundance coming to them?
options: They will fear and be enlarged
questions.correctAnswer: They will fear and be enlarged
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:5 mentions that 'thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged...' indicating a profound emotional and spiritual response to God's blessings.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 60:11 describe the gates of the city?
options: They will be shut at night
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:11 states, 'Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night...' indicating a constant state of welcome and abundance.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 60:19, the sun will be the light by day.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:19 says, 'The sun shall be no more thy light by day...' indicating that God will be the everlasting light instead.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 60:18 states that violence shall be heard in the land.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:18 states, 'Violence shall no more be heard in thy land...' which depicts a future of peace and safety.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:13 say will beautify the place of God's sanctuary?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:13 mentions 'The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee...' indicating the beauty that will be brought to God's sanctuary.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 60:22 speak of growth and multiplication?
options: A little one shall become a thousand
A small one shall remain small
questions.correctAnswer: A little one shall become a thousand
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:22 states, 'A little one shall become a thousand...' which signifies God's ability to bring about great increase and multiplication.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 60:15, God says the people have been forsaken and hated.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:15 states, 'Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated...' confirming the historical challenges faced by God's people.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 60 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 60.

questions.question: What will the LORD bring instead of brass according to Isaiah 60:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:17 states 'For brass I will bring gold,' indicating a transformation of materials to signify abundance and prosperity.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:18, what shall be called Salvation?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:18 states, 'but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation,' indicating the security and divine protection provided to the people.

questions.question: In Isaiah 60:19, who is described as an everlasting light?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:19 says, 'but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light,' emphasizing God's eternal presence and guidance.

questions.question: Which of the following themes is echoed in Revelation 21:23 about the new Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:19's theme of the LORD as light parallels Revelation 21:23, which states the city has no need of the sun or moon, for the glory of God illuminates it.

questions.question: Isaiah 60:20 mentions that the sun shall no more go down. What does this symbolize?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:20 indicates that the sun will not set, symbolizing eternal joy, glory, and the end of suffering, as God will be the everlasting light.

questions.question: What will happen to the people according to Isaiah 60:21?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:21 declares, 'Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever,' signifying a promise of restoration and righteousness.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:22, what will a little one become?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:22 states, 'A little one shall become a thousand,' indicating the exponential growth and blessing of God upon His people.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 60:12 states that nations not serving the people will flourish.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:12 states, 'the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish,' indicating that only those who serve will thrive.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Isaiah 60:18 with the phrases 'walls Salvation' and 'gates Praise'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:18 uses parallelism by stating 'walls Salvation' and 'gates Praise,' reinforcing the themes of security and worship.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 60:7 mentions the rams of Nebaioth ministering unto the people.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:7 states, 'the rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee,' indicating the service and offerings from surrounding nations.

questions.question: What will be made for officers and exactors in Isaiah 60:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:17 declares, 'I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness,' indicating a governance marked by justice and tranquility.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the city of the LORD' in Isaiah 60:14?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:14 refers to 'the city of the LORD' as a testament to the restoration and future glory of Jerusalem, fulfilling God's promises.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event does Isaiah 60:6 recall with the mention of gold and incense?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:6, mentioning gold and incense, foreshadows the gifts brought by the Magi to Jesus in Matthew 2:11, signifying recognition of His kingship.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 60 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 60 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:1 emphasize about the arrival of light?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:1 states, 'for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee,' indicating that the light signifies the glory of God which has been revealed.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Isaiah 60:12 for nations that will not serve the people of God?
options: They will be punished with famine
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:12 warns, 'For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted,' indicating divine judgment on nations that reject God's people.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:3, who will come to the light of God's people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:3 declares that 'the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising,' signifying a gathering of all nations to God's glory.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Isaiah 60:16 regarding His relationship with His people?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 60:16, the phrase 'I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer' emphasizes God’s grace as He offers salvation and restoration.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:18 promise regarding the future state of the land?
options: It will be filled with violence
It will be a place of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a place of peace
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:18 states, 'Violence shall no more be heard in thy land,' indicating a future characterized by peace and safety.

questions.question: What does the multitude of camels in Isaiah 60:6 symbolize?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:6 mentions, 'The multitude of camels shall cover thee... they shall bring gold and incense,' indicating the wealth and abundance that will come to God’s people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 60:14 reflect on the treatment of those who previously afflicted God's people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:14 states that 'the sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee,' showing that former oppressors will recognize and honor God’s people.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 60:19-20 convey about God's presence?
options: God will be their everlasting light
God will allow darkness to prevail
questions.correctAnswer: God will be their everlasting light
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:19-20 states that 'the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light,' emphasizing God's eternal presence and guidance for His people.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:4 suggest about the restoration of the people?
options: Both sons and daughters will be gathered
questions.correctAnswer: Both sons and daughters will be gathered
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:4 expresses that 'thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side,' indicating a complete restoration of both sons and daughters.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 60:10, what change occurs in the relationship between God and His people?
options: God will no longer show mercy
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:10 states that 'their kings shall minister unto thee,' indicating a reversal of fortunes where even kings will serve God's people out of respect for God's mercy.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 60:15 indicate about the transformation of God's people?
options: They will become a joy for generations
questions.correctAnswer: They will become a joy for generations
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:15 promises, 'I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations,' indicating a future of honor and delight for God’s people.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be gained from the combination of Isaiah 60:5 and 60:16?
options: God's people will face eternal judgment
God will provide physical sustenance only
God’s blessings are contingent on human effort
God freely offers salvation and abundance
questions.correctAnswer: God freely offers salvation and abundance
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:5 and 60:16 combined teach that God's grace results in both spiritual and material blessings, as He offers 'salvation' and 'the abundance of the sea.'

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the promises of prosperity in Isaiah are irrelevant to modern believers. What does Isaiah 60:22 actually teach?
options: God's timing is perfect for blessings
The promises are conditional on obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God's timing is perfect for blessings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:22 states, 'I the LORD will hasten it in his time,' affirming that God's promises of prosperity and growth will be fulfilled according to His divine timing.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is reflected in Isaiah 60:17 regarding the transformation of resources?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:17 indicates God's generosity as He promises to exchange 'brass for gold' and 'iron for silver,' demonstrating His willingness to abundantly provide for His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 60:8 contribute to the understanding of God's people in the context of redemption?
options: They will be recognized and valued
They will be ignored by others
They will be rejected by the nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will be recognized and valued
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:8 questions, 'Who are these that fly as a cloud,' indicating that the people of God will be seen as significant and will draw attention from the nations, reflecting their redeemed status.
